articles.detail: 5 cycles, 5 completed, avg 12 published/cycle (59 yesterday); 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. There are no active experiments and no pause gate, but the writer and editor moved from sonnet-5 to sonnet-5-5 today (2026-09-29). Any change started now would be confounded with that swap. The 09-27 plan to revisit on 09-30 now needs clean post-swap days, so hold until about 2026-10-02.
weakestArea: Multi-source share is 26% against a 30% target (16 of 62 articles). It fell for a third day in a row (43%, then 31% by metrics or 29% by audit, then 26%). The count of corroborated stories slipped from 18 to 16, while Dawn (9) and Premium Times Nigeria (6) added single-source regional pieces. The 2026-05-09 floor-3 experiment was reverted and must not be repeated. If it is still under 30% after the model-swap baseline, look at how the selector uses multiSourceStories in politics, where most corroborated stories sit.
watching: Regeni: an Italian court convicted Egyptian officers. It was published twice across cycles, from Al Jazeera on 09-28 and Mada Masr on 09-29, and sameEventDuplicates did not catch it (details in coverageGaps).
Red Sea: the Houthis seized the Bab al-Mandab coast near Mokha, Yanbu loadings resumed, and diesel hit a record in Houston.
Pakistan: the IMF review opened alongside a fuel price cut and a motorcycle subsidy scheme, while Afridi defies Islamabad in Peshawar.
Moldova: Dodon claims Sandu faces impeachment. This story is sourced only from state or advocacy outlets.
Nigeria: NNPC picked Chinese refinery partners, an anti-laundering review is under way, Atiku rebutted a corruption report, and deaths in custody in Minna are being probed.
AI regulation: Anthropic filed an extinction-risk warning, Florida is suing to halt ChatGPT, tech chiefs signed a non-binding pledge, and OpenAI halted its Astra launch.
coverageGaps: sameEventDuplicates reported 0, but the Regeni sentencing ran twice: 2026-09-29-regeni-italy-convicts-egyptian-agents (Al Jazeera, dated 09-28T19:45) and 2026-09-29-regeni-egyptian-officers-sentenced-rome (Mada Masr). They have different outlets, different titles and no shared URL, so the detector missed a cross-cycle pair. Both are still live; one should be removed or merged.

Latin America is at 3%, with Brazil (a science piece) and Stanley (a Falklands oil story datelined in a British territory) and no hard news from mainland Latin America. Yesterday was 7%, so this is one bad day, not a trend.

Six datelines are countries or 'Global', not cities: India, Nigeria, Ukraine, Brazil, United Kingdom, Global. That breaks the city-only location rule mobile's dateline strip relies on, and the missingDateline check does not count it.
Oceania has one story (Perth iron ore), and Pacific coverage is nil.
Freshness was measured on only 9 of 62 articles.
context: All five cycles completed, up from four yesterday, and output rose to 62. The average cycle took 1309s, up from 1242s, and the writer averaged 349s, which could be the first sign of the sonnet-5-5 swap and is worth watching. Science held at 8 across dedicated outlets (Nature, Nature Communications, Phys.org, Mongabay), and US datelines stayed under the cap at 23%. Four stories were state-or-advocacy-only (RT/TASS on Moldova and Mali, Declassified UK, and a Jalud settlers story), up from two.
